questions.question: Which of the following places of Indus Valley Civilization is located in India?
questions.solution:
• Lothal is one of the places of Indus Valley Civilization located presently in India.
 
• It is located near Saragwala, a village in the Ahmedabad district of the state Gujarat.
 
• The word Lothal means “the mount of the dead”.

questions.question: Where did Siddhartha (Buddha) get enlightenment?
questions.solution:
• Siddhartha also was known as Buddha got his enlightenment in Gaya located in the Indian state of Bihar.
 
• Buddha obtained enlightenment under a tree which is now popularly known as the Bodhi Tree.
 
• Bodh Gaya is the most sacred place for the Buddhists.
 
• Buddha achieved Mahaparinirvana around 484 BCE in the town of Kushinagar in north India.
 
• Buddha gave his first sermon in Sarnath.

questions.question: The closest astronomical object to the Earth is ____________.
questions.solution:
• The Moon is the closest astronomical object to the Earth at a distance of 384,400 km.
 
• Proxima Centauri is 40.12 trillion km away from the Earth.
 
• Venus is 261 million kilometers away from the Earth.
 
• The sun is at a distance of 149.6 million km from the earth.

questions.question: Asia's highest mountain peak is ____________.
questions.solution:
• At 8,848m, Mount Everest also is known as Sagarmatha in Nepali, is the highest mountain peak in Asia and also the highest mountain peak in the world.
 
• It is located in the Solukhumbu District of Nepal.

questions.question: Name the representative of the princely states who did **NOT** participate in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
• The representative of Hyderabad state which is a princely state did not attend the Constituent Assembly.
 
• Hyderabad did not want to be a part of India as they wanted to be independent and had lack of trust in the Indian political system.

questions.question: The President's rule has its origin in which of the following nations?
questions.solution:
• The President's rule has its origin in the United States of America and it was introduced so that the Government might fulfill their imperial interests.
 
• Once the President’s rule is imposed on a certain state, the chief minister will not be in power of the state and the Governor of the state who is appointed by the Government will take full control.

questions.question: What type of unemployment at present is a serious threat to the development of the Indian nation?
questions.solution:
**Educated unemployment **is a serious threat to the development of the Indian nation and it is due to the following reasons:

 
• In urban areas especially, the growth of the industrial sector is very low leading the cause of unemployment as jobs are a rarity.
 
• Permanent jobs are also a rarity as it creates a feeling of depression among the students.

questions.question: Cheap Money refers to ____________
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Cheap Money basically refers to a low level of interest rates.**__
 
• It is a monetary policy in which a loan or credit with a low-interest rate is given by a central bank and is ideal for people looking to buy something.
 
• Borrowers can use this cheap money to bet a new loan at a lower interest and pay their existing debts.

questions.question: The chemical property of an element depends on ____________.
questions.solution:
• The chemical properties of an element depend on the atomic number of that element.
 
• The chemical properties depend on the number of the electrons and the configuration of the valence electrons of that element.

questions.question: __________ turns the blue litmus paper into red.
questions.solution:
• **In the presence of an acid**, a blue litmus paper turns into red.
 
• Litmus is **made up of weak organic acid molecule.**
 
• Litmus **acts as an indicator** and it reacts with an acid (H+) and shows a different colour **when it is deprotonated or protonated **under acidic conditions

questions.question: What is measured with the help of decibels?
questions.solution:
• Decibels (dB) is used to measure the loudness of sound i.e. a measure of the intensity of the sound.
 
• It is basically a relative measurement as it relates the intensity of the sound wave to normal pressure.

questions.question: The balloon filled with Hydrogen gets burst when it goes up because of ________.
questions.solution:
• Due to the decrease in air pressure, a balloon filled with Hydrogen gets burst when it goes up in the air.
 
• Hydrogen is a gas lighter than air which helps the balloon to rise up in the air but as it goes up the air pressure around the balloon decreases and it causes the balloon to burst.
 
• To avoid such incidents Helium is used to fill up the balloon which is another gas lighter than air.

questions.question: Which crop is helpful in Nitrogen fixation?
questions.solution:
• Legumes help in the process of Nitrogen fixation.
 
• Bacteria are present in the nodules of the legumes where the process of nitrogen fixation is done by the bacteria and the NH₃ produced is absorbed by the plant.

questions.question: What is the most responsible factor for plant diseases?
questions.solution:
• Plant pathogenic Fungi are the most responsible factor for plant diseases.
 
• Fungi can grow in both living & dead plant tissue.
 
• They can lay dormant until conditions become favorable for their reproduction in both Asexually and sexually.
 
• Fungi diseases vary from attacking the whole plant to specific parts of the plant.
 
• Bacteria is a single cell, a microscopic, prokaryotic organism that shows asexual reproduction and can transmit from one plant to another and in a way transmits the diseases.
 
• Some of the symptoms of bacterial diseases in plants are overgrowth, canker, soft rots, etc.

questions.question: In which form of energy, problem of pollution doesn’t happen?
questions.solution:
• Solar energy does not cause any pollution as it is a natural and conventional source of energy which we directly get from the sun.
 
• Consumption and use of solar energy does not effect the environment.
 
• Plants also use solar energy for photosynthesis.

questions.question: The primary consumer in an ecology chain is: __________.
questions.solution:
• The primary consumer in an ecology chain is the vegetarian, also known as the herbivorous which feeds on plants. For Example- goat, cow.
 
• Carnivorous is considered as the secondary consumers.
 
• Apex predators or alpha predators are considered as the tertiary consumers.

questions.question: The control panel is a part of the _______ in the Computer System.
questions.solution:
• A component of Microsoft Windows, the Control Panel is a software present in the computer system.
 
• It is a part of the graphical user interface of the computer system which provides the ability to change and view various system settings.

questions.question: "Bull Fighting" is the popular sport of which of the following country?
questions.solution:
• Bullfighting is a popular sport in Spain, where it is defined as a cultural event.
 
• It is basically a physical sport which involves animals and humans trying to kill or subdue a bull under a set of guidelines.

questions.question: Which of the following has written "Ashtadhyayi"?
questions.solution:
• "Ashtadhyayi" was written by Panini, a Sanskrit Philogist, who is also known as the “Father of Linguistics”.
 
• "Ashtadhyayi" or “Eight Chapters” written in 6th to 5th century BCE provides knowledge about four thousand rules used in the Sanskrit language.

questions.question: Central Government have approved the investment for how many states under the 'Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation' (AMRUT) scheme in the year 2017?
questions.solution:
• Six states have been approved by the Central Government under the 'Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation' (AMRUT) scheme in the year 2017.
 
• The scheme was launched in June 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to establish an infrastructure that would ensure well-maintained water supply and sewage networks.
 
• The stated under the scheme are Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Telangana.

questions.question: J. A. Fleming is the inventor of which of the following?
questions.solution:
__
 
• John Ambrose Fleming invented the **Diode bulb **__in the year 1904.
 
• Fleming was an English electrical Engineer who also formulated the right-hand law used in physics.

questions.question: The place Maghar is related to which of the great personality?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Maghar **__is related to __**Kabir**__, a famous poet and saint of the 15th century.
 
• Maghar is the place where Kabir breathed his last and has a mausoleum dedicated to him.
 
• Kabir was born in Varanasi. He was a 15th - century Indian mystic poet and saint, whose writings influenced Hinduism's Bhakti movement.
 
• Lumbini is the birthplace of Lord Buddha. It is a place near Kapilavastu in Nepal. He was born in a Shakya Kshatriya family in 563 BC.
 
• Vaishali is the birthplace of __Mahavira Swami.__

questions.question: Who was the first woman who received the Jnanpith award?
questions.solution:
• In 1976, Ashapoorna Devi, a Bengali Novelist became the first woman to receive the Jnanpith award.
 
• She won the award for her novel “Pratham Pratisruti”, published in the year 1964.

questions.question: Which country of Asia launched a rail service to London in 2017?
questions.solution:
• On 1 Jan 2017, China launched a rail service to London, known as the Yiwu-London Railway Line.
 
• The Yiwu-London Railway Line covers a distance of 12,000km from Yiwu, China to London.
